claim: KCC-20 puts the token itself on Kaspa's base layer: with KRC-20 your balance is whatever the Kasplex indexer says, with KCC-20 your balance is what the chain enforces.
why_this_claim: It is the video's marquee contrast (CH3, the C3 two-lane diagram) and it survives cold: no timeline, no status, no token counts, no price. Both sides of the comparison are stated inside the body span itself, so the viewer needs nothing from the other five minutes. Everything else in the video is either dated status (Last Call, superseded by Final on Oct 21), mechanics (the four ideas), drifting numbers (token counts, daily transactions), or Mike's unscripted pitch. The one line that still means the same thing in a month is where the token lives.

spans.says: With KRC-20, token operations are written onto Kaspa as data, and the Kasplex indexer works out who owns that. Your balance is the indexer's answer. With KCC-20, the token state sits inside a covenant UTXO on the base layer, and the chain script enforces every transfer. Your balance is what the chain enforces.

rejected.reason: The CH1 thesis FACE line ('Real tokens on Kaspa's base layer ... not by an off-chain indexer'). It is also redundant with the KCC-20 lane, which says the same thing with the KRC-20 contrast that makes it land.

The Oct 7 receipt line ('pull request 31 merges ... flips to Last Call'). Best visual variety in the video (BR-1 + H0 card, C9 PR receipt, RX4 status diff, BR-2 corridor) but it is dated status, superseded when KCC-1/2/20 went Final on Oct 21, and it carries the news, not the claim. 12.56 s would also leave no room for the contrast.

'The difference is where the token lives.' would have been the ideal bridge into the body, but its onset 132.72 is INSIDE the SPIN marquee transition (lib:spin-center-swinging-cw, 0.84 s on 132.72). Rule 2.

'Now Kaspa already has tokens, KRC-20, from Kasplex, a third party control, live since September 2024.' Carries the misspeak 'control' (script: protocol) left as recorded, and its onset sits on the IMG-3 cross-warp (0.5 s at 117.72). A 30 s short would make the misspeak prominent.

'That is the whole difference.' reads perfectly after 'Your balance is what the chain enforces.' but on screen it is the CLIP-1 LEAD-OUT still (Sivan Helfer's frozen last frame with his burned caption), which means nothing cold, and its out-point 186.38 is inside the MELT window (lib:melt-equidistant-short-2, 0.44 s on 186.44).
